questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose University of Washington in Seattle because it has a very acknowledged creative writing program and because Seattle is known as a liberal city with lots of culture so I figured that I would have fun there. And I had!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A semester as an exchange student not only makes you grow as a person and become very independent, it also pushes you to handle difficult and unforeseen situations all the time, and you experience new things everyday. I would recommend it to anyone who have the opportunity!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The information and help from that students receive from KU is very criticizable. I felt very on my own and I got the sense that the people who are hired to help were bothered by my questions and lacked basic information. I know that many of the other students share my experience. I have ideas to how the process can be improved, and would love to talk with someone about it. Please feel free to contact me if you want me to elaborate further on my experience.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The people who are hired at UW to help the exchange students settle did not do their job. They misinformed me about my tuition which left me with a fee, and they did not answer any emails or questions. I believe that they have found a new system to integrate the exchange students after the summerbreak so hopefully it will be better in the future.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not that difficult. We found an apartment online very close to campus. Though it was expensive and my landlord tried to trick us for extra money all the time so I would probably not recommend it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed living of campus. I shared an apartment with my friend from KU, and it was very nice to have our own kitchen. I know that people who live on campus must eat all their meals in the cafeteria. And I do not think that I could share a room with anyone for such a long time. Would definitely recommend off campus living as it is also in some cases cheaper (at least in Seattle).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We had a good apartment close to campus but our landlord tried to trick us for money all the time. So you have to be aware of that!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I felt that I had some trouble filling out my application and that it was difficult to get help from the UW because the application needed to be filled out during the summer vacation. We also needed to pay 100 dollars in order to get a paper that we needed to apply for a visa. They said that the money covered the costs of an express mail but it took a month before they sent it anyway.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They answered by mail but very slowly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I could only apply for one creative writing class which was very disappointing but the classes that I got were very very good. Exchange students are not prioritized but that I think that is pretty fair because the exchange semester is about so much more than the academia.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Students who apply to UW must be aware that the application shall be sent during KU's summer vacation. KU did not inform us about this the first time I applied and I almost missed the deadline. We were specifically told that there would be no deadlines before the new semester started and I only realized it because I got a mail from UW. The people who were supposed to help us from KU were on vacation and we needed some papers from them. It was very criticizable.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My classes were so great and I have learned so much.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was a MA student at KU but took BA classes at UW.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is so much more homework during the semester than at KU, and attendance is also very common. The final exams are shorter though. The grading system was also very different.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I took three literature courses my first quarter. One about modernism, one about surrealism and one about the reader as a participant in meaning creation. My las quarter I had a creative writing course and a literature course about the printing press. They were all so good and I have learned so much!

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I only had good experiences with my courses and teachers. All the professors were so nice and helpful and the classes were so intersting. I guess people just need to apply for courses that seem interesting to them!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than I expected. I had lived in the US before but the prices were so high now. I guess Seattle is an expensive city. I spent a lot of money on traveling. We flew out two times to visit other states. I would recommend to save some money up for this.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive but transportation in Seattle is only about a 50 dollars pr quarter (3 months) if you are a student so I saved a lot of money on that.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UW is such a huge campus and you can do about anything there. They even have a bowling alley on campus and so many different types of sports and clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I guess you can do anything a UW. They offer so many clubs and activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: We went line dancing on a country bar once a week. That was very fun. I know that some people did Salsa and rock climbing too. You can do any type of sport.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend that you rent a car and drive out to see some of the nature surrounding Seattle. It is so beautiful. 

There is a company called ScanDesign who arrange events for danish exchange students. New students must get in touch with them! They are so nice and everything is free!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is difficult to say. I guess you never really get used to a culture that is so different from your own. Things and people kept surprising me but that is the fun of a exchange semester. And I settled pretty quickly. I guess you do that when you know that you only have 6 months in the new place.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: My classmates were not so open to be friends so I guess the best way would be to join a club or a sport.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I guess one of the biggest cultural differences is the gun law. I never felt unsafe because of it but it is wired that people there have such a fundamental different view. Seattle is pretty liberal but there are still some political differences as well. And I hate that every time you need help from a company you must talk to a robot or like three different people. It is so difficult to just solve basic problems with for instance an internet provider. New students must be aware of this!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I love the English language and I really like how there are so many different cultures in Seattle. And the nature there is so beautiful. I am a huge fan of the US, and this exchange semester has only made me more of a fan!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Bring a mastercard. We had so much trouble paying with our danish cards. You must bring a master card and get an american card. Chase was not a good bank, I have heard good things about American Express. And bring a second danish card to keep in your house if you loose your wallet (that happened to me and it sucked).

2. You must pick a housing that already has internet because it was so difficult to find a provider who would give internet to a non US citizen (I do not know why but it was). 

3. Don't bring so much stuff or clothes. You can buy it when you are there and you want to be able to bring a lot of things home. 

4. Travel as much as you can. You have such a great opportunity to see the country and in country flights are pretty cheap.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: See my answer above

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the travling that I got to do. And also that I got to experience college life. Overall I just had a great time and I am so grateful that I got the opportunity to do this!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: We had so much trouble with things such as getting internet access and renting cars. I do not know why it is so difficult to be a foreigner in the US, but you must be aware of this. I guess it helps if you have a mastercard and an American Express card.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
